## What changed

**A failed step said everything except what went wrong.** On a real machine the
climb stopped with:

```
ОСТАНОВЛЕНО: шаг не выполнился — exec-failed code=100
argv=apt-get -c /var/lib/gitlab-upgrade/apt-proxy.2130032.conf update
```

Which command, which exit code — and not one word about what apt actually
said. The reason had been sitting in `err.result.stderr` the whole time and was
simply never printed, leaving a person with exit 100 and nothing to fix. The
`ExecError` message is deliberately machine-readable for the journal; the
screen now gets the command, its code, and the line the command itself
produced:

```
ОСТАНОВЛЕНО: шаг не выполнился — apt-get … update → 100:
E: The repository '…focal InRelease' is not signed.
```

Warnings no longer crowd out the error. apt prints `W: GPG error…` above
`E: The repository … is not signed`, and the first-matching-line rule picked
the complaint instead of the diagnosis. An `E:` line now wins; where there is
nothing but warnings they are still shown, because saying something beats
saying nothing.

The line is passed through URL redaction before it is shown: apt will happily
print a proxy URL in full, password included, and this text goes to the screen,
the journal, and a phone notification.
